metadata.title: Theory of Constraints Foundations — Sources
metadata.description: Primary books and references for 11 TOC primitives: five focusing steps, drum-buffer-rope, throughput accounting, evaporating cloud, current/future reality trees, prerequisite and transition trees, critical chain, policy constraints, and thinking processes. Includes software/DevOps lineage (Phoenix Project, DevOps Handbook, Flow Framework) and 2025 empirical literature.

books.name: The Goal: A Process of Ongoing Improvement
books.description: Goldratt, E.M. & Cox, J. (1984). The foundational TOC text. Source for Five Focusing Steps (primitive 01) and the TOC system concept. 3rd revised edition 2004.

books.name: The Race
books.description: Goldratt, E.M. & Fox, R.E. (1986). Introduces Drum-Buffer-Rope and flow-based production scheduling. Source for primitive 02 (DBR).

books.name: The Haystack Syndrome: Sifting Information Out of the Data Ocean
books.description: Goldratt, E.M. (1990). Introduces Throughput Accounting (T, I, OE framework) and the distinction from cost accounting. Source for primitive 03 (Throughput Accounting) and primitive 10 (Policy Constraints).

books.name: It's Not Luck
books.description: Goldratt, E.M. (1994). Introduces the full Thinking Processes suite: Evaporating Cloud, CRT, FRT, PRT, TT. Source for primitives 04–08 and 11.

books.name: Critical Chain
books.description: Goldratt, E.M. (1997). Introduces Critical Chain Project Management (CCPM), Project Buffer, Feeding Buffer, and buffer management. Source for primitive 09.

books.name: The Constraints Management Handbook
books.description: Cox, J.F. & Spencer, M.S. (1998). CRC Press/St. Lucie Press. Comprehensive reference for all TOC concepts including 5FS, DBR, TA, and Thinking Processes. Source for all 11 primitives.

books.name: Throughput Accounting
books.description: Corbett, T. (1998). North River Press. Dedicated treatment of T/I/OE measurement, T/CU product mix decisions, and the comparison with cost accounting. Source for primitive 03.

books.name: Project Management in the Fast Lane: Applying the Theory of Constraints
books.description: Newbold, R.C. (1998). St. Lucie Press. Practical CCPM application including buffer sizing, critical chain identification, and resource buffers. Source for primitive 09.

books.name: Thinking for a Change: Putting the TOC Thinking Processes to Work
books.description: Scheinkopf, L.J. (1999). CRC Press. Practitioner guide to applying all five Thinking Processes. Source for primitive 11 and detailed application guidance for primitives 04–08.

books.name: Critical Chain Project Management
books.description: Leach, L.P. (2000). Artech House. Comprehensive CCPM implementation guide including S-DBR for project management. Source for primitive 09.

books.name: Manufacturing at Warp Speed: Optimizing Supply Chain Financial Performance
books.description: Schragenheim, E. & Dettmer, H.W. (2001). CRC Press. Advanced DBR and policy constraint application in supply chain and operations. Source for primitives 02 and 10.

books.name: The Logical Thinking Process: A Systems Approach to Complex Problem Solving
books.description: Dettmer, H.W. (2007). ASQ Quality Press. The most comprehensive academic treatment of all five Thinking Processes including Categories of Legitimate Reservation. Source for primitives 04–08 and 11.

books.name: Supply Chain Management at Warp Speed: Integrating the System from End to End
books.description: Schragenheim, E., Dettmer, H.W. & Patterson, J.W. (2009). CRC Press. Introduces Simplified DBR (S-DBR). Source for primitive 02.

books.name: Beyond the Goal: Eliyahu Goldratt Speaks on the Theory of Constraints
books.description: Goldratt, E.M. (2005). Audio/book collection covering TOC applications to services, projects, and distribution. Background reference for all 11 primitives.

books.name: The Phoenix Project: A Novel About IT, DevOps, and Helping Your Business Win
books.description: Kim, G., Behr, K. & Spafford, G. (2013). IT Revolution Press. The primary text translating Goldratt's Three Ways and TOC constraint logic into IT operations and software delivery. Explicitly modeled on The Goal; introduced 'The Four Types of Work' and the Three Ways (flow, feedback, continual learning). 500,000+ copies sold. Source for software/DevOps application of 5FS, DBR, and Policy Constraints.

books.name: The DevOps Handbook: How to Create World-Class Agility, Reliability, and Security in Technology Organizations
books.description: Kim, G., Humble, J., Debois, P. & Willis, J. (2016). IT Revolution Press. Second edition 2021. Formalizes 'The First Way' (flow) as direct application of TOC constraint logic to software delivery pipelines. The industry-standard bridge between Goldratt's manufacturing model and DevOps practice. Source for software/DevOps application of 5FS, DBR, and throughput accounting.

books.name: Project to Product: How to Survive and Thrive in the Age of Digital Disruption with the Flow Framework
books.description: Kersten, M. (2018). IT Revolution Press. Introduces the Flow Framework, which maps TOC's Five Focusing Steps onto software value streams. Defines four Flow Items (features, defects, risks, debt) and five Flow Metrics (velocity, time, efficiency, load, distribution). Treats the value stream as the drum in a DBR-equivalent model. Source for software application of 5FS (primitive 01) and DBR (primitive 02) via Flow Load as the buffer signal.

books.name: Flow Engineering: From Value Stream Mapping to Effective Action
books.description: Pereira, S. & Davis, A. (2024). IT Revolution Press. 304 pages. Five-map workshop methodology grounded in Value Stream Mapping, cybernetics, and the Toyota Production System. Operationalizes TOC constraint identification in software and knowledge-work contexts; connects to CRT and 5FS via collaborative mapping. 2026 Axiom Book Awards Gold Medal winner. Source for applied VSM-as-constraint-identification in software delivery.

books.name: Systematic Review on the Use of CCPM in Project Management: Empirical Applications and Trends
books.description: de Oliveira Martins, Benetti, dos Anjos, da Silva & Alves (2025). Applied Sciences, 15(15), 8147, published 2025-07-22. DOI: 10.3390/app15158147. Systematic literature review analyzing 62 CCPM studies from Scopus and Web of Science (2014–2025). Key findings: most studies use simulation/modeling rather than field trials; construction and manufacturing dominate; growing integration trend with Scrum, Lean Construction, and predictive algorithms. Strongest peer-reviewed evidence base for primitive 09, but establishes active favourable simulation research — not field effect sizes in knowledge work. Note: mdpi.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetching; full author list, volume, issue, article number and publication date verified via Crossref API 2026-08-14, findings taken from the published abstract. The 19.3% construction time reduction figure cited in some summaries derives from a separate 2023 MDPI Buildings study — not a finding of this review.

books.name: A framework for using Theory of Constraints thinking processes and tools to complement qualitative system dynamics modelling
books.description: Mabin, V.J. & Cavana, R.Y. (2024). System Dynamics Review (Wiley), 40(4), e1768, published 2024-03-14. DOI: 10.1002/sdr.1768. Proposes a six-stage framework combining TOC Thinking Processes (CRT) with qualitative system dynamics (Qual SD) modelling, arguing the combination yields more collective insight than either method alone. Peer-reviewed. Applies to complex multi-stakeholder constraint scenarios that resist single-root CRT analysis. Note: Wiley returns HTTP 402 to automated fetching; exact title, volume, issue, article number and date verified via Crossref API 2026-08-14 (this corrects an earlier note in this file that volume/issue could not be confirmed). Full text paywalled — the claimed advantage is reported from the abstract, not independently assessed.

articles.name: 2025 State of AI-assisted Software Development Report
articles.description: DORA / Google Cloud (2025). Global survey of ~5,000 technology professionals conducted 13 June – 21 July 2025, plus qualitative data. The strongest available survey evidence for the AI-era constraint shift: ~90% AI adoption; higher AI adoption is associated with an increase in BOTH software delivery throughput and software delivery instability; time saved during code generation is reallocated to verification overhead, moving the constraint from writing code to reviewing and verifying it. Also introduces seven team profiles (including a 'legacy bottleneck' profile) and frames AI as an amplifier of existing organizational strengths and dysfunctions. Evidence grade: large-N correlational survey, not a controlled trial. Verified 2026-08-14 that no 2026 DORA report had been published — 2025 is the most recent. Report PDF: https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/2025_state_of_ai_assisted_software_development.pdf. Source for the post-AI-adoption 5FS re-run trigger.

articles.name: Agent-X: Full Pipeline Acceleration of On-device AI Agents
articles.description: Chung, J., Shin, B., Kim, J. & Rhu, M. (KAIST, 2026). arXiv:2605.10380v1, 11 May 2026. Measured end-to-end latency breakdown of an on-device agent (Mac mini, M4 Pro): Planner 43.5% and Arbiter 46.9% of total latency (together 90.4%); decode 68.7%, prefill 21.7%. Critically, the paper states this CONTRASTS with cloud/server-class LLM workloads where decode is overwhelmingly dominant (>95%). Cited in this skill as the corrected provenance for the previously over-generalized '~70% Planner/Arbiter decode' claim — the split is on-device-specific and does not transfer to cloud pipelines. Evidence grade B+: measured systems research on a specific deployment, not a general law.

articles.name: Act While Thinking: Accelerating LLM Agents via Pattern-Aware Speculative Tool Execution
articles.description: Sui, Y., Zhao, H., Ma, R., He, Z., Wang, H., Li, J. & Yang, Y. (2026). arXiv:2603.18897v1, 19 March 2026. Identifies the strictly serialized LLM-generation → tool-execution loop as the dominant latency bottleneck in tool-heavy agent workloads: tool execution accounts for ~60% of request time in coding tasks, ~50% in deep research, ~36% in scientific research. Proposes speculative tool execution (predicting and pre-running likely tool calls while the LLM still generates) — a TOC-legible exploitation move on the constraint stage before adding capacity. Source for the agent-pipeline constraint analysis recipe: demonstrates the constraint stage is deployment-dependent and must be profiled, not assumed.

articles.name: The Revenge of QA: How AI Code Generation Is Exposing Decades of Process Debt
articles.description: Brown, L. (January 2026). IT Revolution. Practitioner synthesis framing AI-driven code review bottleneck as a direct TOC/5FS problem: code creation is not the constraint — verification, code review, and integration are. References 'Revenge of QA' (Hendrickson, Fredrick, Enochs, Willis, Kazempour; Enterprise Technology Leadership Journal, Fall 2025). Evidence grade B: practitioner synthesis, not peer-reviewed RCT.

articles.name: The Shifting Bottleneck Conundrum: How AI Is Reshaping the Software Development Lifecycle
articles.description: Logilica (December 9, 2025). Independent practitioner analysis of AI-driven code review bottleneck. Key claims: 67% of developers use AI for coding yet merge approvals remain 77% human-controlled; median engineer at large company takes ~13 hours to merge a PR; teams using AI-assisted review see 30% faster merge approvals. Corroborates the constraint-shift pattern now better evidenced by DORA 2025 (see DORA2025AIAssisted) and IT Revolution (2026). Evidence grade B: vendor-published observational data, not RCT — prefer DORA 2025 as the primary citation and use this only as corroboration.

articles.name: Executive Control of Cognitive Processes in Task Switching
articles.description: Rubinstein, J.S., Meyer, D.E. & Evans, J.E. (2001). Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance, 27(4), 763-797. DOI: 10.1037/0096-1523.27.4.763. Peer-reviewed, replicated experimental evidence that task switching imposes a measurable time cost, increasing with rule complexity and decreasing with advance cuing. Independent cognitive-psychology research, not a TOC or CCPM study — cited in this skill as mechanism-level corroboration for Critical Chain's anti-multitasking guidance, not as validation of Goldratt's specific throughput-loss percentages. Source for primitive 09 (Critical Chain) evidence-grading section.
